# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).

- [Terse Comments Only](feedback_terse_comments.md) — One short line max, only for non-obvious WHY; stop writing multi-line prose comments in code/config even though CLAUDE.md already says this.

- [Never Hard-Wrap Prose](feedback_never_hard_wrap_prose.md) — PR descriptions and all Markdown: one line per paragraph, never manual line breaks.
- [Succinct Written Artifacts](feedback_succinct_written_artifacts.md) — Changesets, PR bodies, docs: short, plain, no AI slop or backstory.
- [No Session Links](feedback_no_session_links.md) — Never put claude.ai session URLs/Claude-Session trailers in commits or PRs; public repo, private sessions.

- [Use gh stack](feedback_use_gh_stack.md) — stacked PRs must be native GitHub stacks (gh stack link); plain chained PRs get no CI.

    fix: report a file Callisto cannot read or look up instead of treating it as missing
    
    Discovery, config, `pre.json`, changelog, apply and init treated any failed read or failed `exists()` as "not there": an unreadable or non-UTF-8 manifest dropped its package from the release, an unsearchable directory made `pre.json` or `callisto.toml` look absent, apply read a failed lookup as a deleted file, and a changeset entry that could not be inspected fell out of the version bump. `callisto_model::strict_fs` now separates a missing path from a failed look, and those sites use it. A manifest that cannot be read is a coded error (E310) under the same admitted-or-warn rule as one that cannot be parsed. The two changeset listings are one strict implementation. `atomic_write` returns a failed directory sync instead of reporting a durable replace it could not confirm.

Review of e7a9e6918 (read-only; no cargo run, nothing executed). Behavior below is traced from source and from the Rust 1.98.1 std error mapping on disk. The findings ledger `../callisto-findings/FINDINGS.md` does not exist, so nothing was skipped as already logged.

## Findings, most severe first

**1. Medium (CONFIRMED): workspace membership and root detection still treat an unreadable manifest as absent, so discovery admits everything and only warns.**
- Sites:
  - `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:175` (`Err(_) => return Membership::absent()`), `:370` (`package_json_declares_name`), `:398` (pnpm-workspace.yaml, `.ok()?`), `:413` (package.json workspaces, `.ok()?`).
  - `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/root.rs:38` (`cargo_document`, `.ok()`) and `:66-67` (`exists()` plus `if let Ok`).
- Failing state: root `Cargo.toml` has `[workspace] members=["crates/*"] exclude=["crates/internal"]` and is unreadable (Latin-1 byte or EACCES).
  - `read_membership` returns `absent()`, which admits every directory.
  - The root's own `admits_explicitly` is false, so the new `ManifestFailure::Unreadable` for the root only prints a warning.
  - Excluded and non-member crates are discovered and released. Exit is 0.
- The same applies to a root `package.json` with `workspaces`, and to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
- For root detection, `is_workspace_root` returns false for an unreadable root `Cargo.toml`. `find_workspace_root` then returns a different ancestor, a nested package root, or `WorkspaceRootNotFound`.
- This is the exact swallow shape the commit set out to remove. The new `WS-DISC-03` sentence "Only a manifest that does not exist is treated as absent" is false for these reads. A parse failure of the root manifest already behaved this way, but the commit text and spec now claim read failures are never skipped.
- Fix: have `read_membership` and the npm readers return `Result`, using `strict_fs::read_optional`, and surface `ManifestReadError`.

**2. Medium (CONFIRMED): dangling `.md` symlinks now abort the changeset listing.**
- Site: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:81`. `fs::metadata(&path)?` is called for every `*.md` entry.
- The old code used `path.is_file()`, which skipped these entries.
- Failing state: Emacs lock file `.changeset/.#foo.md`, a dangling symlink whose extension is `md`.
  - `status`, `version` and `check_partial_run` now fail with "No such file or directory".
- Same failure if a changeset is deleted between `readdir` and `metadata` (`NotFound`).
- `changeset_listing_errors_on_an_entry_it_cannot_inspect` pins the dangling-symlink case as intended.
- Fix: treat `NotFound` from `metadata` as skip. Keep other errors fatal.

**3. Low-Medium (CONFIRMED): the entry that failed is not named, and the new changeset says it is.**
- Sites: `aggregate.rs:104-107` and `commands/version.rs` (`working_tree_has_pending_changeset`, the new `.map_err`). Both set `path` to the changesets directory and `message` to the bare `io::Error` text.
- The `read_dir` entry error and the `metadata` error never include the entry path.
- The old `version.rs` code did name `changesets_dir.join(name)`, so this is a diagnostic regression.
- Failing state: a changeset with a permission or symlink problem gives "No such file or directory (os error 2)" with only the directory shown.
- Fix: have `list_changeset_files` attach the entry path to the error.

**4. Medium (CONFIRMED mechanism, PLAUSIBLE filesystem triggers): `atomic_write` can now fail after the rename, and `probe_atomic_write` does not cover the new failure.**
- Site: `crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs:43-48` and `:59-63`.
- `release execute` (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs:514`) probes the receipt destination before the first effect, so a receipt write cannot fail after landed effects.
- `probe_atomic_write` (`atomic.rs:77-92`) only does `create_dir_all` plus a temp file. It never opens or syncs the directory.
- Failing states:
  - Parent directory mode `-wx` (for example 0o311). `File::open(dir)` returns EACCES, but the temp file and rename succeeded. The command errors after the registry publish, although the receipt is on disk.
  - macOS or FUSE filesystems where directory `fsync` returns `ENOTSUP`. On darwin `ENOTSUP` (45) differs from `EOPNOTSUPP` (102), and std maps only `EOPNOTSUPP` to `Unsupported`, so `ENOTSUP` becomes `Uncategorized` and is not exempted.
  - `EBADF` or `EISDIR` from odd filesystems are also not exempted.
- Other callers that error after the file is already replaced:
  - `apply.rs:184` returns before `modified_paths.push(rel_pre_path)`, so a rewritten `pre.json` is left unstaged.
  - Manifest writers report failure for a file that has changed.
- Suggested fix: call `sync_directory(parent)` in the probe. Consider treating a failed open for read or an unsupported fsync as best-effort, and only hard-fail on `EIO`/`ENOSPC`-style errors.
- When `create_dir_all` creates several levels, only the immediate grandparent is synced. This is no worse than before.
- Not a regression: Windows (`#[cfg(not(unix))]` is a no-op, and the old code ignored the open failure there) and a genuinely read-only checkout (the write itself would fail first).

**5. Low (CONFIRMED): `apply.rs` strict lookups now run after side effects, and TOCTOU remains.**
- `apply.rs:223` (lockfile loop) and `:232-238` (partition) run after manifests and `pre.json` were written and lockfiles refreshed. A lookup failure there, for example an `ELOOP` lockfile symlink, aborts a half-applied run that previously succeeded.
- The `path_exists` plus `fs::remove_file` pair (around `:257-263`) is still racy. `remove_file` returning `NotFound` is a hard error.
- Suggested fix: do the lookups in a preflight, and call `remove_file` directly, ignoring `NotFound`.
- Lockfile detection at `apply.rs:558, 560, 568, 580, 589, 598, 607, 615` still uses `.exists()`. A failed lookup silently skips the refresh. The later `path_exists` at `:223` then errors for the lockfiles in its list, but only after other refreshes ran.

**6. Medium-Low (CONFIRMED): sibling sites with the same shape, missed by this commit (item 4 of the brief).**

`exists()` followed by a read, or a read error swallowed into a decision:
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:87` and `:155`. Failed lookup returns `Ok(None)`, so a package drops silently from the matrix.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs:30`. A failed lookup means `continue`, so a group's napi targets are silently omitted. `:114` is `abs_path.exists()` driving a diagnostic.
- `crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:208-212`. `exists()` then `if let Ok(..)` and `.ok()`: an unreadable root `Cargo.toml` makes `cargo_workspace` `None`, so `version.workspace = true` inheritance is silently unresolved.
- `crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:626, 629, 632, 637-638`. `detect_npm_workspace_kind` uses `exists()` and `if let Ok`. `:85` is `read_to_string(..).ok()?`, which falls back to a `workspace:` name.
- `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:261, 266-273`. Auto-binary discovery uses `read_dir` with `if let Ok`, `.flatten()` and `is_file()`. An unreadable `src/bin` or `src/main.rs` silently drops binary targets from the release-asset decision.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:523`. `init_files` still calls `.exists()` for `README.md`, while `write_changeset_readme` (`:560`) is now strict. Dry-run reports a different file list than the real run.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:585`. `changesets_config_diagnostics` uses `let Ok(..) else return`. This only affects diagnostics.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/root.rs:55` and `:76`, and `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:871-872`. `.is_file()` and `.exists()` guards.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:71-77` treats only `NotFound` as an empty listing. `strict_fs` also treats `NotADirectory` as absent, so the two are inconsistent when a changesets path has a file as a parent. This is cosmetic.
- AGENTS.md says to sweep structurally identical code or track it. The commit has no record of what it deliberately left. Fix by migrating these sites or tracking them. The plan note "No lint ban on exists()/ok()" is the only trace.

## Tests that would still pass with the fix reverted

- `a_directory_sync_failure_is_reported` (`atomic.rs`). It calls `sync_directory` directly on a missing path. Reverting the `?` in `atomic_write` leaves it green. Nothing tests the grandparent-only-when-created rule or the swallowing of `Unsupported`/`InvalidInput`.
- Every `LockedDir::lock` test returns early with `None` as root or on non-unix, so it is vacuously green there (typical CI containers). These are `a_path_that_cannot_be_looked_up_is_an_error_not_a_deletion`, `init_guards_report_a_file_they_cannot_look_up...`, `a_config_that_cannot_be_looked_up_is_an_error_not_the_default`, and the `strict_fs` test `an_unreadable_file_or_unsearchable_parent_is_an_error_not_absence`.
- No test covers these converted sites:
  - `commands/version.rs` pre.json reads in `plan_version` and `check_partial_run`.
  - `cli/commands/pre.rs` enter and exit.
  - `changelog/write.rs` `prepend` read failure.
  - the `apply.rs` deferred-deletion branch.
  - `working_tree_has_pending_changeset` error propagation.
  - `load_changesets_permissive` propagating a `list_changeset_files` error.
- Discovery: nothing asserts that an unreadable non-member manifest warns and does not error, or that the sibling-admitted branch returns `ManifestReadError`. Only the message string is tested, and the explicit-member case and the directory-as-manifest case are tested. Turning `Unreadable` into always-error or always-warn for non-members would pass.
- The two tests that do bite are `an_unreadable_manifest_explicitly_admitted_by_its_own_ecosystem_errors` and `a_manifest_that_is_a_directory_in_an_admitted_member_errors`. The old `let Ok else continue` would have skipped both.

## Docs, spec and error-code consistency

- `ARCHITECTURE.md:12` still says "then `fsync` the parent and grandparent directories". The grandparent is now synced only when the call created the parent, and failures now propagate.
- Per AGENTS.md ("change the spec in the same PR as the behavior"), the changes below are not in any spec. The `docs/specs/versioning.json` criterion on pre.json fails with E114/E115 (`:174`) and the one on writes (`:212`) are the nearest candidates. The changes without a spec update are:
  - strict `callisto.toml` and `pre.json` reads;
  - the changeset listing error;
  - `atomic_write` failing on directory sync.
- `WS-DISC-03` in `docs/specs/workspace.json` ("Only a manifest that does not exist is treated as absent") is overbroad (see finding 1). The code also treats `NotADirectory` as absent.
- `docs/errors.md` E310 and the `LocateError` help text match each other. E310 skips E306-E309, which are unused anywhere in the tree. The E209 row is not cross-referenced. This is consistent otherwise.
- `GraphError::PreJsonRead` (`error.rs:263`) hardcodes ".changeset/pre.json" and ignores a configured `changesets_dir`. The configured path is not in the message. This was already the case before the commit.

## Checked and fine

- `read_optional`/`exists`: only `NotFound` and `NotADirectory` are absent. `ELOOP` (`FilesystemLoop`), `EACCES`, `EISDIR` and `InvalidData` are errors. A dangling symlink is `NotFound`, which is absent, same as before. `path.try_exists()` returns `Ok(false)` for `NotFound`. `is_absent` covers `NotADirectory` for a path beneath a regular file.
- `pre enter` and `pre exit`: the converted branches match the old behavior. A missing `pre.json` gives a fresh state on enter and `PreNotActive` on exit. The `Io` path is the correct `pre_path`.
- `plan_version` and `check_partial_run`: the `if let Some(text)` branch runs only when the file exists, and the errors map to `PreJsonRead`.
- `config::load`: `ConfigError::Read` carries the right path, and a missing file gives the default.
- Changelog `prepend`: `ReadFailed` is correct, and a missing file gives the template. A dangling symlink behaves as before.
- Init guards: the paths and the `InitIo` mapping are right.
- `list_changeset_files`: the `README.md` exclusion and the `.md` extension are equivalent to the old filters (the `config.json`/`pre.json` exclusions were redundant). Directories named `x.md` are skipped. A symlinked changesets directory works because `read_dir` follows it. A symlink to a file is included, whereas `working_tree_has_pending_changeset` formerly used `file_type()` and excluded it. That change is minor and arguably a fix.

## Findings, most severe first

**1. Medium (CONFIRMED): workspace membership and root detection still treat an unreadable manifest as absent, so discovery admits everything and only warns.**
- Sites:
  - `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:175` (`Err(_) => return Membership::absent()`), `:370` (`package_json_declares_name`), `:398` (pnpm-workspace.yaml, `.ok()?`), `:413` (package.json workspaces, `.ok()?`).
  - `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/root.rs:38` (`cargo_document`, `.ok()`) and `:66-67` (`exists()` plus `if let Ok`).
- Failing state: root `Cargo.toml` has `[workspace] members=["crates/*"] exclude=["crates/internal"]` and is unreadable (Latin-1 byte or EACCES).
  - `read_membership` returns `absent()`, which admits every directory.
  - The root's own `admits_explicitly` is false, so the new `ManifestFailure::Unreadable` for the root only prints a warning.
  - Excluded and non-member crates are discovered and released. Exit is 0.
- The same applies to a root `package.json` with `workspaces`, and to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
- For root detection, `is_workspace_root` returns false for an unreadable root `Cargo.toml`. `find_workspace_root` then returns a different ancestor, a nested package root, or `WorkspaceRootNotFound`.
- This is the exact swallow shape the commit set out to remove. The new `WS-DISC-03` sentence "Only a manifest that does not exist is treated as absent" is false for these reads. A parse failure of the root manifest already behaved this way, but the commit text and spec now claim read failures are never skipped.
- Fix: have `read_membership` and the npm readers return `Result`, using `strict_fs::read_optional`, and surface `ManifestReadError`.

**2. Medium (CONFIRMED): dangling `.md` symlinks now abort the changeset listing.**
- Site: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:81`. `fs::metadata(&path)?` is called for every `*.md` entry.
- The old code used `path.is_file()`, which skipped these entries.
- Failing state: Emacs lock file `.changeset/.#foo.md`, a dangling symlink whose extension is `md`.
  - `status`, `version` and `check_partial_run` now fail with "No such file or directory".
- Same failure if a changeset is deleted between `readdir` and `metadata` (`NotFound`).
- `changeset_listing_errors_on_an_entry_it_cannot_inspect` pins the dangling-symlink case as intended.
- Fix: treat `NotFound` from `metadata` as skip. Keep other errors fatal.

**3. Low-Medium (CONFIRMED): the entry that failed is not named, and the new changeset says it is.**
- Sites: `aggregate.rs:104-107` and `commands/version.rs` (`working_tree_has_pending_changeset`, the new `.map_err`). Both set `path` to the changesets directory and `message` to the bare `io::Error` text.
- The `read_dir` entry error and the `metadata` error never include the entry path.
- The old `version.rs` code did name `changesets_dir.join(name)`, so this is a diagnostic regression.
- Failing state: a changeset with a permission or symlink problem gives "No such file or directory (os error 2)" with only the directory shown.
- Fix: have `list_changeset_files` attach the entry path to the error.

**4. Medium (CONFIRMED mechanism, PLAUSIBLE filesystem triggers): `atomic_write` can now fail after the rename, and `probe_atomic_write` does not cover the new failure.**
- Site: `crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs:43-48` and `:59-63`.
- `release execute` (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs:514`) probes the receipt destination before the first effect, so a receipt write cannot fail after landed effects.
- `probe_atomic_write` (`atomic.rs:77-92`) only does `create_dir_all` plus a temp file. It never opens or syncs the directory.
- Failing states:
  - Parent directory mode `-wx` (for example 0o311). `File::open(dir)` returns EACCES, but the temp file and rename succeeded. The command errors after the registry publish, although the receipt is on disk.
  - macOS or FUSE filesystems where directory `fsync` returns `ENOTSUP`. On darwin `ENOTSUP` (45) differs from `EOPNOTSUPP` (102), and std maps only `EOPNOTSUPP` to `Unsupported`, so `ENOTSUP` becomes `Uncategorized` and is not exempted.
  - `EBADF` or `EISDIR` from odd filesystems are also not exempted.
- Other callers that error after the file is already replaced:
  - `apply.rs:184` returns before `modified_paths.push(rel_pre_path)`, so a rewritten `pre.json` is left unstaged.
  - Manifest writers report failure for a file that has changed.
- Suggested fix: call `sync_directory(parent)` in the probe. Consider treating a failed open for read or an unsupported fsync as best-effort, and only hard-fail on `EIO`/`ENOSPC`-style errors.
- When `create_dir_all` creates several levels, only the immediate grandparent is synced. This is no worse than before.
- Not a regression: Windows (`#[cfg(not(unix))]` is a no-op, and the old code ignored the open failure there) and a genuinely read-only checkout (the write itself would fail first).

**5. Low (CONFIRMED): `apply.rs` strict lookups now run after side effects, and TOCTOU remains.**
- `apply.rs:223` (lockfile loop) and `:232-238` (partition) run after manifests and `pre.json` were written and lockfiles refreshed. A lookup failure there, for example an `ELOOP` lockfile symlink, aborts a half-applied run that previously succeeded.
- The `path_exists` plus `fs::remove_file` pair (around `:257-263`) is still racy. `remove_file` returning `NotFound` is a hard error.
- Suggested fix: do the lookups in a preflight, and call `remove_file` directly, ignoring `NotFound`.
- Lockfile detection at `apply.rs:558, 560, 568, 580, 589, 598, 607, 615` still uses `.exists()`. A failed lookup silently skips the refresh. The later `path_exists` at `:223` then errors for the lockfiles in its list, but only after other refreshes ran.

`exists()` followed by a read, or a read error swallowed into a decision:

- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:523`. `init_files` still calls `.exists()` for `README.md`, while `write_changeset_readme` (`:560`) is now strict. Dry-run reports a different file list than the real run.
